title: Chogha Zanbil (Dur-Untash)
summary: Chogha Zanbil, in Khuzestan, Iran, was founded around 1250 BCE by the Elamite king Untash-Napirisha as the religious centre of Elam. Its ziggurat originally measured 105.2 m a side and about 53 m high in five levels. The city stayed unfinished and was destroyed by the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal about 640 BCE.

uncertainty.note: Start is the foundation c. 1250 BCE (UNESCO; ICOMOS); UNESCO dates the founder Untash-Napirisha to 1275-1240 BCE. The city was destroyed about 640 BCE; the ruins remain, so the end is the present.

reviewer_note: Shape ziggurat. The 105.2 m side and about 53 m height are UNESCO's figures for the ziggurat as originally built; the 53 m is an estimate, since UNESCO says the ruin now stands only 24.75 m high. The ICOMOS evaluation (poorly OCRed) gives the c. 1250 BC foundation and reign dates of 1265-1245 BC for Untash-Napirisha, which differ from UNESCO's 1275-1240.
